docs.title: MCP Java SDK
docs.text:
The Java SDK for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the open protocol that connects AI applications to tools and data. Use it to build MCP clients and MCP servers in Java 17 or later, with a synchronous or an asynchronous API.

The SDK implements two generations of the protocol, side by side in the same module:

  • Modern, for the stateless 2026-07-28 specification, where every request stands alone.
  • Legacy, for the 2025-11-25 specification and earlier revisions, where client and server keep a session.

The names are the specification's own, and legacy does not mean deprecated here: the SDK supports both. See Modern or Legacy? to choose between them.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
What each implementation supports:

Feature Modern Legacy Tools: discovery, calls, structured output Yes Yes Resources and URI templates Yes Yes Prompts Yes Yes Completions for argument values Yes Yes Elicitation: asking the user for input Yes, as a multi round-trip request (form and URL) Yes, as a request from the server Sampling Server only Yes Roots Server only Yes Progress notifications Yes Yes Logging No (deprecated by the revision) Yes Change notifications Yes, with subscriptions/listen Yes, over the session Finding out what a server supports server/discover initialize handshake Caching hints on results Yes No Custom HTTP headers for tool arguments (SEP-2243) Yes No

Both implementations share the following:

  • Sync and async APIs. Choose blocking calls or Project Reactor types.
  • Transports without a web framework. STDIO, and Streamable HTTP on the JDK HttpClient (client) and the Servlet API (server). The legacy implementation also has the deprecated SSE transport.
  • Pluggable JSON serialization. Jackson 3.x by default, or Jackson 2.x.
  • Security hooks. Pluggable authorization hooks, and opt-in DNS rebinding protection with Host/Origin header validation (see HTTP Transport Security).

Spring applications

Spring WebFlux and WebMVC transports for the legacy client and server are part of Spring AI 2.0+ and are not shipped by this SDK. Use the MCP Client Boot Starter and the MCP Server Boot Starter from Spring AI. For the modern client and server, Spring AI 2.1+ provides Boot starters and Spring transports; see MCP Client Boot Starter and MCP 2026-07-28 Servers. Also consider the MCP Annotations and MCP Security.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Add the mcp module, which bundles the core SDK with Jackson 3.x JSON serialization:

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk</groupId>
    <artifactId>mcp</artifactId>
</dependency>

The Quickstart covers versions, the BOM, Gradle, and the other modules.

docs.title: MCP Client (2026-07-28)
docs.text:
Note

The modern client is available since 2.2.0. Its API, in the io.modelcontextprotocol.modern packages, may change in minor releases until 3.0, and some parts of the revision are not implemented. For servers of earlier revisions, use the legacy client.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The modern client talks to servers of the stateless 2026-07-28 MCP specification revision. It lives in io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client, next to the legacy client, and shares no types with it: it has its own McpClient, its own McpSchema, and its own transports. Both ship in mcp-core, so no extra dependency is needed.

The 2026-07-28 revision removes sessions and the initialize handshake. Every request carries the protocol version and the client's capabilities in its _meta. The modern client is built around that:

  • Nothing to initialize. Building a client does no I/O. The first request goes out when the first call starts.
  • One client per user. A client stands for one identity. It is cheap to create, so an application that serves several users creates one client per user. See Identity and Authorization.
  • Shared transports. A transport keeps no state about calls. Many clients can share one transport, and so one connection pool. A client does not own its transport; whoever created the transport closes it.
  • Immutable request specs. Each operation starts from a spec, for example client.tool("echo").arguments(args).call(). Every setter returns a new spec, so a configured spec can be kept and reused.
  • The protocol details are handled for you. The client adds the _meta block, negotiates the protocol version, answers the server's input requests, and sets the Mcp-* headers.

docs.title: Modern or legacy?
docs.text:
Modern client Legacy client Package io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client io.modelcontextprotocol.client Spec revision 2026-07-28 2025-11-25 and earlier Startup None initialize() handshake Sessions No Yes Elicitation Input request answered in a retry of the call Server-to-client request Sampling, roots Not supported Supported Logging Not supported (deprecated by the revision) Supported

The modern client only speaks the 2026-07-28 protocol version. It cannot call servers that expect an initialize handshake.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
A client that lists the server's tools and calls one over HTTP:

SyncAsync 
import java.util.Map;

import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.CallToolResult;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.Implementation;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.Tool;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.McpClient;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.McpSyncClient;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.transport.HttpClientMcpTransport;

HttpClientMcpTransport transport = HttpClientMcpTransport.builder("http://localhost:8080/mcp").build();

McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .clientInfo(Implementation.builder("my-client", "1.0.0").build())
    .build();

for (Tool tool : client.listTools().list().tools()) {
    System.out.println(tool.name());
}

CallToolResult result = client.tool("echo")
    .arguments(Map.of("text", "Hello"))
    .call();
System.out.println(result.content());

import java.util.Map;

import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.CallToolResult;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.Implementation;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.McpAsyncClient;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.McpClient;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.transport.HttpClientMcpTransport;

HttpClientMcpTransport transport = HttpClientMcpTransport.builder("http://localhost:8080/mcp").build();

McpAsyncClient client = McpClient.async(transport)
    .clientInfo(Implementation.builder("my-client", "1.0.0").build())
    .build();

CallToolResult result = client.listTools().list()
    .doOnNext(tools -> tools.tools().forEach(tool -> System.out.println(tool.name())))
    .then(client.tool("echo")
        .arguments(Map.of("text", "Hello"))
        .call())
    .block(); // block() only to keep the example short
System.out.println(result.content());

Clients are immutable and thread-safe. There is nothing to start and nothing to close on the client.

Builder options:

Method Purpose clientInfo(Implementation) The client's name and version, sent in _meta of every request. Optional, but recommended. roundTimeout(Duration) Timeout of one network exchange. Defaults to 20 seconds. See Timeouts. callTimeout(Duration) Bound on a whole call. None by default. See Timeouts. formElicitation(...) / urlElicitation(...) Handlers that answer the server's input requests. See Elicitation. progress(...) Listener for progress notifications. See Progress. transportContextProvider(Supplier) Sync only. The identity of each call. See Identity and Authorization. maxInputRounds(int) How many times a call answers input requests before it fails. Defaults to 10. maxListPages(int) How many pages a listing of all pages reads before it fails. Defaults to 100. jsonMapper(McpJsonMapper) JSON mapper. Defaults to McpJsonDefaults.getMapper().

docs.title: Streamable HTTP
docs.text:
HttpClientMcpTransport uses the JDK HttpClient. Every request is a POST to the MCP endpoint, answered with one JSON response or with an event stream scoped to that request. Waiting for an answer holds no thread.

HttpClientMcpTransport transport = HttpClientMcpTransport.builder("https://example.com/mcp")
    .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
    .customizeClient(http -> http.sslContext(sslContext))
    .build();
Method Purpose connectTimeout(Duration) How long establishing a connection may take. Defaults to 10 seconds. customizeClient(Consumer<HttpClient.Builder>) Customize the HttpClient, for example its executor or SSL context. clientBuilder(HttpClient.Builder) Replace the HttpClient builder. HTTP/1.1 is used by default. requestCustomizer(McpHttpRequestCustomizer) Add headers to each request. Customizers run in the order they were added. authorizationErrorHandler(McpHttpAuthorizationErrorHandler) Decide whether a request answered with 401 or 403 is sent again. maxResponseSize(int) Maximum bytes of one response body or one streamed event. Defaults to 16 MiB. jsonMapper(McpJsonMapper) JSON mapper. Defaults to McpJsonDefaults.getMapper().

Note

Set the connect timeout with connectTimeout(...) on the transport builder. A connect timeout set on the HttpClient builder through customizeClient or clientBuilder is replaced by the transport's value.

docs.title: STDIO
docs.text:
StdioMcpClientTransport runs the server as a process and exchanges newline-delimited JSON-RPC over its standard streams.

SyncAsync 
import io.modelcontextprotocol.client.transport.ServerParameters;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.transport.StdioMcpClientTransport;

ServerParameters params = ServerParameters.builder("java")
    .args("-jar", "my-mcp-server.jar")
    .build();

try (StdioMcpClientTransport transport = StdioMcpClientTransport.builder(params).start()) {
    McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport).build();
    // use the client
}

import io.modelcontextprotocol.client.transport.ServerParameters;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.transport.StdioMcpClientTransport;

ServerParameters params = ServerParameters.builder("java")
    .args("-jar", "my-mcp-server.jar")
    .build();

try (StdioMcpClientTransport transport = StdioMcpClientTransport.builder(params).start()) {
    McpAsyncClient client = McpClient.async(transport).build();
    // use the client
}

start() spawns the process. Clients never start or close the transport they are given, so one process can serve several clients; close the transport once they are done. When the server's output ends or the transport is closed, every open call fails with McpResponseLostException.

StdioMcpClientTransport.builder(InputStream, OutputStream) runs over streams that are already connected, such as a socket's.

docs.title: Spring
docs.text: Spring Boot integration for the modern client is part of Spring AI 2.1+, not of this SDK. Its MCP Client Boot Starter configures modern connections and exposes their tools to Spring AI as tool callbacks. See MCP Client Boot Starter in the Spring AI reference.

docs.title: Custom Transports
docs.text:
Other transports implement McpClientTransport. Its single method, exchange(McpTransportRequest), sends one request and emits the server's notifications followed by exactly one response.

An HTTP transport built on another HTTP client can reuse the SDK's building blocks: McpHttpRequestHeaders.forRequest(request) returns the headers the revision requires, request.withRoundTimeout(...) applies the round timeout to one attempt, and McpHttpRequest.builder(...) and McpHttpResponseInfo.of(...) create the values the request customizers and the authorization error handler receive.

docs.title: Sync and Async
docs.text:
McpClient.sync(transport) builds an McpSyncClient, and McpClient.async(transport) builds an McpAsyncClient. Both offer the same operations.

  • Sync calls run on the calling thread and return the result. Elicitation handlers run on that thread too.
  • Async calls return a Mono (or a Flux for listen streams). Nothing is sent before subscription. Handlers return a Mono and must not block.
SyncAsync 
McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport).build();

CallToolResult result = client.tool("echo")
    .arguments(Map.of("text", "Hello"))
    .call();
System.out.println(result.content());

McpAsyncClient client = McpClient.async(transport).build();

client.tool("echo")
    .arguments(Map.of("text", "Hello"))
    .call()
    .subscribe(result -> System.out.println(result.content()));

The examples on this page have a Sync and an Async tab. Choosing one switches all of them.

docs.title: Calling the Server
docs.text:
Every operation takes two steps:

  1. A method on the client starts the request. It sends nothing yet; it returns a request spec, on which you set arguments and per-call settings.
  2. A final method on the spec sends the request and returns the result (in the async client, a Mono of it).

In client.tool("echo").arguments(args).call(), tool("echo") starts the request and call() sends it.

Operation Start the request Send it Call a tool client.tool(name) or client.tool(Tool) call() Read a resource client.resource(uri) read() Get a prompt client.prompt(name) get() Complete an argument client.completion(ref, argument, value) complete() List one page client.tools(), prompts(), resources(), resourceTemplates() list() List all tools client.listTools() list() Discover the server client.discover() Sent right away; there is nothing to configure Listen for changes client.listen() open(listener) (sync), events() (async) SyncAsync 
ReadResourceResult resource = client.resource("file:///config.json").read();

GetPromptResult prompt = client.prompt("greeting")
    .arguments(Map.of("name", "Ada"))
    .get();

CompleteResult completion = client.completion(new PromptReference("greeting"), "name", "A").complete();
List<String> suggestions = completion.completion().values();

Mono<ReadResourceResult> resource = client.resource("file:///config.json").read();

Mono<GetPromptResult> prompt = client.prompt("greeting")
    .arguments(Map.of("name", "Ada"))
    .get();

Mono<List<String>> suggestions = client.completion(new PromptReference("greeting"), "name", "A")
    .complete()
    .map(completion -> completion.completion().values());

A tool failure the model should see is not an exception. It is a CallToolResult whose isError() is true.

docs.title: Per-Call Settings
docs.text:
A spec starts from the client's settings. Each setter replaces one of them for that call only:

SyncAsync 
CallToolResult result = client.tool("generate_report")
    .arguments(Map.of("year", 2026))
    .roundTimeout(Duration.ofMinutes(5))
    .progress(progress -> System.out.println(progress.message()))
    .meta(Map.of("com.example/traceId", traceId))
    .call();

Mono<CallToolResult> result = client.tool("generate_report")
    .arguments(Map.of("year", 2026))
    .roundTimeout(Duration.ofMinutes(5))
    .progress(progress -> Mono.fromRunnable(() -> System.out.println(progress.message())))
    .meta(Map.of("com.example/traceId", traceId))
    .call();

meta(...) adds entries to the request's _meta. It rejects progressToken and keys starting with io.modelcontextprotocol/, which the client sets itself.

docs.title: Listing and Pagination
docs.text:
The list specs return one page. Pass the previous page's nextCursor() to read the next one:

SyncAsync 
String cursor = null;
do {
    ListResourcesResult page = client.resources().cursor(cursor).list();
    page.resources().forEach(resource -> System.out.println(resource.uri()));
    cursor = page.nextCursor();
}
while (cursor != null);

Flux<Resource> resources = client.resources().list()
    .expand(page -> page.nextCursor() == null ? Mono.empty()
            : client.resources().cursor(page.nextCursor()).list())
    .flatMapIterable(ListResourcesResult::resources);

For tools, client.listTools().list() reads all pages and returns them as one result.

docs.title: The Kept Tool Listing
docs.text:
The client keeps the result of listTools().list() for as long as the server's ttlMs allows, and returns it without asking the server again.

  • client.listTools().skipCache().list() always asks the server and keeps the new listing.
  • client.tools().list(), which reads one page, always asks the server.
  • A listing with a ttlMs of 0 is not kept.
  • A listen stream that tracks tool changes drops the kept listing when the tools change.
  • A listing the server marks as private is kept too, because a client stands for one user.

docs.title: Server Discovery
docs.text:
client.discover() returns the server's supported versions, capabilities and instructions. The result is kept for its ttlMs.

SyncAsync 
DiscoverResult server = client.discover();
ServerCapabilities capabilities = server.capabilities();
Object serverInfo = server.meta() != null ? server.meta().get(McpSchema.MetaKeys.SERVER_INFO) : null;

client.discover().subscribe(server -> {
    ServerCapabilities capabilities = server.capabilities();
    Object serverInfo = server.meta() != null ? server.meta().get(McpSchema.MetaKeys.SERVER_INFO) : null;
});

The server's name and version are not a field of the result. Servers send them in _meta, under io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo, as an untyped map. A server may leave _meta out, so check for null.

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
Timeout Bounds Default Round timeout One network exchange: from sending a request until its response arrives. 20 seconds Call timeout The whole call: every exchange, every handler and every wait. None
  • Progress notifications do not extend the round timeout. A tool that runs longer than the round timeout fails unless you raise it, on the builder or on the call's spec.
  • The call timeout includes the time a user takes to answer an elicitation, so a slow user fails the call. Use it where a hard deadline matters more, for example in unattended jobs.
  • Listen streams have no timeout.

A timeout fails the call with McpTimeoutException, whose kind() is ROUND or CALL. The request may have reached the server, so its outcome is unknown. The client never retries it.

docs.title: Elicitation
docs.text:
The 2026-07-28 revision has no server-to-client requests. A server that needs input from the user answers a tools/call, resources/read or prompts/get with an input_required result. The client asks its handlers and sends the request again with the answers, until the server completes it. See Multi Round-Trip Requests for the server side.

sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Application
    participant Client as MCP client
    participant Handler as Elicitation handler
    participant Server as MCP server

    App->>Client: tool("deploy").arguments(args).call()
    Client->>Server: tools/call
    Server-->>Client: input_required (input requests, requestState)
    Client->>Handler: elicit(request)
    Handler-->>Client: ElicitResult
    Client->>Server: tools/call with inputResponses and requestState
    Server-->>Client: CallToolResult
    Client-->>App: CallToolResult

The application makes one call and gets one result. The rounds in between are the client's job.

SyncAsync 
McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .formElicitation(request -> {
        String name = askUser(request.message(), request.requestedSchema());
        return name != null ? ElicitResult.accept(Map.of("name", name)) : ElicitResult.decline();
    })
    .urlElicitation(request -> {
        boolean opened = askConsentAndOpenBrowser(request.message(), request.url());
        return opened ? ElicitResult.accept(Map.of()) : ElicitResult.decline();
    })
    .build();

McpAsyncClient client = McpClient.async(transport)
    .formElicitation(request -> askUser(request.message(), request.requestedSchema())
        .map(name -> ElicitResult.accept(Map.of("name", name)))
        .defaultIfEmpty(ElicitResult.decline()))
    .urlElicitation(request -> askConsentAndOpenBrowser(request.message(), request.url())
        .map(opened -> opened ? ElicitResult.accept(Map.of()) : ElicitResult.decline()))
    .build();
  • Form mode. The handler receives an ElicitFormRequest with a message and a JSON schema, and returns the user's answer.
  • URL mode. The handler receives an ElicitUrlRequest. Ask the user for consent, open the URL, and return right away. The server learns from the browser when the user is done. The request that follows an accepted URL elicitation has no round timeout, because the server may hold it open until then.
  • Per call. formElicitation(...) and urlElicitation(...) on a tool, resource or prompt spec replace the client's handler for that call.
  • Capabilities follow the handlers. Each request declares the elicitation capability for exactly the modes that have a handler. A client without handlers declares none.
  • Threads. A sync handler runs on the thread that made the call. A timeout cannot interrupt it; the call timeout is checked when the handler returns. An async handler returns a Mono, which is cancelled when the call ends without its answer; close any pending dialog then.

A call answers input requests at most maxInputRounds times (10 by default) and then fails with McpInputRoundsExceededException.

docs.title: Running the Rounds Yourself
docs.text:
callOnce(), readOnce() and getOnce() send the request once and return the server's answer as it is: the final result or an InputRequiredResult. Use them to pause a call, for example until a user answers in a later HTTP request, and continue it with inputResponses(...) and requestState(...):

SyncAsync 
McpSyncClient.ToolSpec deploy = client.tool("deploy").arguments(Map.of("env", "prod"));

CallToolOutcome outcome = deploy.callOnce();
if (outcome instanceof InputRequiredResult inputRequired) {
    Map<String, Object> responses = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    inputRequired.inputRequests().forEach((key, request) -> responses.put(key, answer(request)));

    CallToolResult result = deploy
        .inputResponses(responses)
        .requestState(inputRequired.requestState())
        .call();
}

McpAsyncClient.ToolSpec deploy = client.tool("deploy").arguments(Map.of("env", "prod"));

Mono<CallToolResult> result = deploy.callOnce().flatMap(outcome -> {
    if (outcome instanceof InputRequiredResult inputRequired) {
        Map<String, Object> responses = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        inputRequired.inputRequests().forEach((key, request) -> responses.put(key, answer(request)));

        return deploy
            .inputResponses(responses)
            .requestState(inputRequired.requestState())
            .call();
    }
    return Mono.just((CallToolResult) outcome);
});

Key the answers as the server keyed its requests, and send requestState back as it was received.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
A progress listener receives the notifications/progress of a call. Set one for every call on the builder, or for one call on its spec:

SyncAsync 
McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .progress(progress -> System.out.println(progress.progress() + " / " + progress.total()))
    .build();

McpAsyncClient client = McpClient.async(transport)
    .progress(progress -> Mono.fromRunnable(
            () -> System.out.println(progress.progress() + " / " + progress.total())))
    .build();
  • The client asks the server for progress only while a listener is in effect.
  • A listener receives the notifications of a call one at a time and in order.
  • A sync listener runs on a thread that may block, not on the calling thread. The call returns after the listener has seen every notification sent before the result.
  • An async listener is a Function<ProgressParams, Mono<Void>>. The next notification and the result wait for the Mono it returns.

docs.title: Change Notifications
docs.text:
client.listen() opens a subscriptions/listen stream. Choose what to listen for on the spec:

Method Event toolsChanged() SubscriptionEvent.ToolsListChanged promptsChanged() SubscriptionEvent.PromptsListChanged resourcesChanged() SubscriptionEvent.ResourcesListChanged resourceUpdates(uri...) SubscriptionEvent.ResourceUpdated, with the resource's uri(), which may be a sub-resource of a subscribed URI

Every stream starts with SubscriptionEvent.Subscribed. Its missing() lists what the server will not report; poll for those instead. Changes made before Subscribed may have been missed, so list again what you keep.

SyncAsync 
McpSyncClient.Listening listening = client.listen()
    .toolsChanged()
    .resourceUpdates("file:///config.json")
    .open(event -> {
        if (event instanceof SubscriptionEvent.ToolsListChanged) {
            refreshTools(client.listTools().list());
        }
        else if (event instanceof SubscriptionEvent.ResourceUpdated updated) {
            reload(updated.uri());
        }
    });

// later
listening.close();

open(...) returns without waiting for the server. The listener runs on a thread that may block, so it may call the client. McpSyncSubscriptionListener also has onError and onComplete, which tell how the stream ended.

Disposable listening = client.listen()
    .toolsChanged()
    .events()
    .retryWhen(Retry.backoff(Long.MAX_VALUE, Duration.ofSeconds(1)))
    .subscribe(event -> handle(event));

Events are emitted on transport threads, so code that reacts to them must not block. retryWhen subscribes again after every failure, including an authorization failure, so filter the errors you want to retry. Add repeat() to subscribe again when the server ends the stream.

A stream ends when the server or the network ends it:

  • it completes when the server ends it with a result, for example on shutdown;
  • it fails with McpSubscriptionLostException when it breaks, so changes may be missed until you listen again.

To keep listening, open the stream again. Each new stream starts with Subscribed again.

A stream that tracks tool changes also keeps the client's tool listing current: the client drops the kept listing on Subscribed and on ToolsListChanged.

docs.title: Identity and Authorization
docs.text:
A client stands for one user. Identity is not an argument of the client's methods. It travels as an McpTransportContext from the call to the transport's hooks, which add it to the HTTP request.

flowchart LR
    A["Client for Alice"] -- "context: Alice" --> T
    B["Client for Bob"] -- "context: Bob" --> T
    T["Shared transport<br/>one connection pool"] --> H["Request customizers<br/>add the caller's token"]
    H --> S["MCP server"]

1. Supply the context of a call.

SyncAsync 
McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .transportContextProvider(() -> McpTransportContext.create(Map.of("user", user)))
    .build();

The provider is called on the calling thread when a call starts or a listen stream opens.

client.tool("echo")
    .arguments(Map.of("text", "Hello"))
    .call()
    .contextWrite(ctx -> ctx.put(McpTransportContext.KEY, McpTransportContext.create(Map.of("user", user))));

2. Use it in the transport's hooks. A hook may block (wrapped with fromSync) or return a Mono. Either kind works with both clients.

SyncAsync 
HttpClientMcpTransport transport = HttpClientMcpTransport.builder("https://example.com/mcp")
    .requestCustomizer(McpHttpRequestCustomizer.fromSync((request, headers, context) ->
        headers.set("Authorization", "Bearer " + tokens.accessToken(context.get("user")))))
    .authorizationErrorHandler(McpHttpAuthorizationErrorHandler.fromSync((request, response, context) -> {
        tokens.refresh(context.get("user"));
        return true; // send the request again
    }))
    .build();

HttpClientMcpTransport transport = HttpClientMcpTransport.builder("https://example.com/mcp")
    .requestCustomizer((request, headers, context) -> tokens.accessToken(context.get("user"))
        .doOnNext(token -> headers.set("Authorization", "Bearer " + token))
        .then())
    .authorizationErrorHandler((request, response, context) -> tokens.refresh(context.get("user"))
        .thenReturn(true)) // send the request again
    .build();
  • Request customizers run before every attempt, including the retry after an authorization error, so a refreshed token is picked up.
  • The authorization error handler is asked when the server answers 401 or 403. It returns true to send the request again, at most maxRetries() times (once by default). Without a handler, or when it returns false, the call fails with McpHttpStatusException.
  • Hooks may run on any thread, and the attempts of one call may run on different threads. Read the identity from the context argument, not from thread-locals.
  • fromSync(...) hooks run on a thread that may block, for example to fetch a token. An exception thrown by a hook reaches the caller as it is.

Share transports, not clients

The client keeps the tool listing and the server/discover result per client, not per user. If one client serves several users, for example with a transportContextProvider that reads the current user from a thread-local, one user can receive a listing that was fetched for another.

Create one client per user over a shared transport. Share a client between users only when the server shows every user the same tools, or use listTools().skipCache().

docs.title: Custom Headers (SEP-2243)
docs.text:
A tool can ask clients to mirror selected arguments into HTTP headers by marking them with x-mcp-header in its input schema (see Custom Headers on the server side). Over HTTP the client sends those arguments as Mcp-Param-{Name} headers. To do so it needs the tool's definition:

  • client.tool(name) uses the definition from the client's earlier listings. If the client has not seen the tool yet, it lists all tools first.
  • client.tool(Tool) uses the definition you pass, so nothing is looked up.
  • When the server rejects the headers with -32020, the client lists the tools again and sends the call once more.
  • A tool the server does not list, or whose annotations are invalid, is not called. The call fails with IllegalArgumentException, and such tools are left out of listTools().

Over STDIO there are no headers, and none of this applies.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
A call that reached the server, or may have, fails with one of two types: McpException for an error the server answered, and McpClientException for a failure in the client or on the way.

Exception Meaning McpException The server answered with a JSON-RPC error. error() has its code, message and data. McpMissingClientCapabilityException An McpException for -32021: the request needs a client capability the call did not declare, for example an elicitation handler. McpTimeoutException A round or call timeout expired. See Timeouts. McpResponseLostException The exchange broke after the request may have reached the server. McpHttpStatusException The server answered with an HTTP error status and no JSON-RPC error, or with a 401 or 403 that was not sent again. statusCode(), headers() and body() have the answer. McpInputHandlerMissingException The server asked for input no handler of the call covers. McpInputRoundsExceededException The server kept asking for input after maxInputRounds. McpInvalidResultException The server's result cannot be accepted, or a listing did not end within maxListPages. McpSubscriptionLostException A listen stream ended without a result from the server.

All but the first two extend McpClientException: the call failed in the client or on the way to the server.

After McpTimeoutException or McpResponseLostException, whether the server acted on the request is unknown. The client never retries such a request; retry it yourself only if the operation is safe to repeat.

Failures outside those two types:

  • Connection failures. A connection that cannot be established, for example a ConnectException or an HttpConnectTimeoutException, is not an McpClientException. The request never reached the server, so it is safe to send again. The async client signals the exception as it is. The sync client throws a RuntimeException with the original exception as its cause.
  • Exceptions from your hooks. An exception thrown by a request customizer or an authorization error handler reaches the caller as it is.
  • IllegalArgumentException, over HTTP, for a tool the server does not list or whose x-mcp-header annotations are invalid.
  • IllegalStateException when an elicitation handler returns no answer.
  • CancellationException when the thread of a sync call is interrupted.

docs.title: Not Yet Supported
docs.text:
• Sampling and roots input requests. The client declares neither capability.
  • Logging, which the 2026-07-28 revision deprecates.
  • Extensions, including Tasks.
  • Servers of earlier revisions. Use the legacy client for those.
  • Obtaining OAuth tokens. Add tokens with a request customizer, as shown in Identity and Authorization.

For a larger working example, see the modern conformance client, which passes the non-auth 2026-07-28 client conformance scenarios.

docs.title: MCP Client
docs.text:
The MCP Client is a key component in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) architecture, responsible for establishing and managing connections with MCP servers. It implements the client-side of the protocol, handling:

  • Protocol version negotiation to ensure compatibility with servers
  • Capability negotiation to determine available features
  • Message transport and JSON-RPC communication
  • Tool discovery and execution with optional schema validation
  • Resource access and management
  • Prompt system interactions
  • Optional features like roots management, sampling, and elicitation support
  • Progress tracking for long-running operations

Tip

The core io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp module provides STDIO, SSE, and Streamable HTTP client transport implementations without requiring external web frameworks.

The Spring-specific WebFlux transport (mcp-spring-webflux) is now part of Spring AI 2.0+ (group org.springframework.ai) and is no longer shipped by this SDK. See the MCP Client Boot Starter documentation for Spring-based client setup.

2026-07-28 specification

This page covers the legacy client, which implements the 2025-11-25 specification and earlier revisions. A client for the stateless 2026-07-28 revision is also available; see MCP Client (2026-07-28).

The client provides both synchronous and asynchronous APIs for flexibility in different application contexts.

Sync APIAsync API 
// Create a sync client with custom configuration
McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .requestTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .capabilities(ClientCapabilities.builder()
        .roots(true)       // Enable roots capability
        .sampling()        // Enable sampling capability
        .elicitation()     // Enable elicitation capability
        .build())
    .sampling(request -> new CreateMessageResult(response))
    .elicitation(request -> new ElicitResult(ElicitResult.Action.ACCEPT, content))
    .build();

// Initialize connection
client.initialize();

// List available tools
ListToolsResult tools = client.listTools();

// Call a tool
CallToolResult result = client.callTool(
    CallToolRequest.builder("calculator")
        .arguments(Map.of("operation", "add", "a", 2, "b", 3))
        .build()
);

// List and read resources
ListResourcesResult resources = client.listResources();
ReadResourceResult resource = client.readResource(
    ReadResourceRequest.builder("resource://uri").build()
);

// List and use prompts
ListPromptsResult prompts = client.listPrompts();
GetPromptResult prompt = client.getPrompt(
    GetPromptRequest.builder("greeting").arguments(Map.of("name", "Spring")).build()
);

// Add/remove roots
client.addRoot(new Root("file:///path", "description"));
client.removeRoot("file:///path");

// Close client
client.closeGracefully();

// Create an async client with custom configuration
McpAsyncClient client = McpClient.async(transport)
    .requestTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .capabilities(ClientCapabilities.builder()
        .roots(true)       // Enable roots capability
        .sampling()        // Enable sampling capability
        .elicitation()     // Enable elicitation capability
        .build())
    .sampling(request -> Mono.just(new CreateMessageResult(response)))
    .elicitation(request -> Mono.just(new ElicitResult(ElicitResult.Action.ACCEPT, content)))
    .toolsChangeConsumer(tools -> Mono.fromRunnable(() -> {
        logger.info("Tools updated: {}", tools);
    }))
    .resourcesChangeConsumer(resources -> Mono.fromRunnable(() -> {
        logger.info("Resources updated: {}", resources);
    }))
    .promptsChangeConsumer(prompts -> Mono.fromRunnable(() -> {
        logger.info("Prompts updated: {}", prompts);
    }))
    .progressConsumer(progress -> Mono.fromRunnable(() -> {
        logger.info("Progress: {}", progress);
    }))
    .build();

// Initialize connection and use features
client.initialize()
    .flatMap(initResult -> client.listTools())
    .flatMap(tools -> {
        return client.callTool(CallToolRequest.builder("calculator")
            .arguments(Map.of("operation", "add", "a", 2, "b", 3))
            .build());
    })
    .flatMap(result -> {
        return client.listResources()
            .flatMap(resources ->
                client.readResource(ReadResourceRequest.builder("resource://uri").build())
            );
    })
    .flatMap(resource -> {
        return client.listPrompts()
            .flatMap(prompts ->
                client.getPrompt(GetPromptRequest.builder("greeting")
                    .arguments(Map.of("name", "Spring"))
                    .build())
            );
    })
    .flatMap(prompt -> {
        return client.addRoot(new Root("file:///path", "description"))
            .then(client.removeRoot("file:///path"));
    })
    .doFinally(signalType -> {
        client.closeGracefully().subscribe();
    })
    .subscribe();

docs.title: Client Transport
docs.text: The transport layer handles the communication between MCP clients and servers, providing different implementations for various use cases. The client transport manages message serialization, connection establishment, and protocol-specific communication patterns.

docs.title: STDIO
docs.text:
Creates transport for process-based communication using stdin/stdout:

ServerParameters params = ServerParameters.builder("npx")
    .args("-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything", "dir")
    .build();
McpTransport transport = new StdioClientTransport(params, McpJsonDefaults.getMapper());

docs.title: Streamable HTTP
docs.text:
Streamable HttpClientStreamable WebClient (external)

Creates a Streamable HTTP client transport for efficient bidirectional communication. Included in the core mcp module:

McpTransport transport = HttpClientStreamableHttpTransport
    .builder("http://your-mcp-server")
    .endpoint("/mcp")
    .build();

The Streamable HTTP transport supports:

  • Resumable streams for connection recovery
  • Configurable connect timeout
  • Custom HTTP request customization
  • Multiple protocol version negotiation

Creates Streamable HTTP WebClient-based client transport. Requires the mcp-spring-webflux dependency from Spring AI 2.0+ (group org.springframework.ai):

McpTransport transport = WebFluxSseClientTransport
    .builder(WebClient.builder().baseUrl("http://your-mcp-server"))
    .build();

docs.title: SSE HTTP (Deprecated)
Protocol Version Negotiation
docs.text:
During initialize(), the client sends the list of protocol versions its transport supports (newest first) and the server picks one it also supports. The negotiated version is returned on the InitializeResult:

McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport).build();

InitializeResult initResult = client.initialize();
String negotiatedVersion = initResult.protocolVersion();

Built-in transports (StdioClientTransport, HttpClientStreamableHttpTransport, HttpClientSseClientTransport) advertise every protocol version the SDK understands (2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25) via their default protocolVersions() implementation, so negotiation normally settles on the newest version both sides support. To restrict a custom transport to a specific subset of versions, override protocolVersions() on your McpClientTransport implementation:

public class RestrictedTransport extends StdioClientTransport {
    // ...
    @Override
    public List<String> protocolVersions() {
        return List.of("2025-06-18"); // only negotiate this version
    }
}

If the server responds with a version the transport didn't advertise, initialize() fails with an McpError.

docs.title: Client Capabilities
docs.text:
The client can be configured with various capabilities:

var capabilities = ClientCapabilities.builder()
    .roots(true)       // Enable filesystem roots support with list changes notifications
    .sampling()        // Enable LLM sampling support
    .elicitation()     // Enable elicitation support (form and URL modes)
    .build();

You can also configure elicitation with specific mode support:

var capabilities = ClientCapabilities.builder()
    .elicitation(true, false)  // Enable form-based elicitation, disable URL-based
    .build();

docs.title: Roots Support
docs.text:
Roots define the boundaries of where servers can operate within the filesystem:

// Add a root dynamically
client.addRoot(new Root("file:///path", "description"));

// Remove a root
client.removeRoot("file:///path");

// Notify server of roots changes
client.rootsListChangedNotification();

The roots capability allows servers to:

  • Request the list of accessible filesystem roots
  • Receive notifications when the roots list changes
  • Understand which directories and files they have access to

docs.title: Sampling Support
docs.text:
Sampling enables servers to request LLM interactions ("completions" or "generations") through the client:

// Configure sampling handler
Function<CreateMessageRequest, CreateMessageResult> samplingHandler = request -> {
    // Sampling implementation that interfaces with LLM
    return new CreateMessageResult(response);
};

// Create client with sampling support
var client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .capabilities(ClientCapabilities.builder()
        .sampling()
        .build())
    .sampling(samplingHandler)
    .build();

This capability allows:

  • Servers to leverage AI capabilities without requiring API keys
  • Clients to maintain control over model access and permissions
  • Support for both text and image-based interactions
  • Optional inclusion of MCP server context in prompts

docs.title: Elicitation Support
docs.text:
Elicitation enables servers to request additional information or user input through the client. This is useful when a server needs clarification or confirmation during an operation:

// Configure form elicitation handler
Function<ElicitFormRequest, ElicitResult> formElicitationHandler = request -> {
    // Present the request to the user and collect their response
    // The request contains a message and a schema describing the expected input
    Map<String, Object> userResponse = collectUserInput(request.message(), request.requestedSchema());
    return new ElicitResult(ElicitResult.Action.ACCEPT, userResponse);
};

// Configure URL elicitation handler
Function<ElicitUrlRequest, ElicitResult> urlElicitationHandler = request -> {
    // Prompt the user to visit the URL
    // e.g. openBrowser(request.url());
    return new ElicitResult(ElicitResult.Action.ACCEPT, Map.of());
};

// Create client with elicitation support
var client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .capabilities(ClientCapabilities.builder()
        .elicitation(true, true) // enables both form and URL elicitation
        .build())
    .elicitation(formElicitationHandler)
    .urlElicitation(urlElicitationHandler)
    .build();

The ElicitResult supports three actions:

  • ACCEPT - The user accepted and provided the requested information
  • DECLINE - The user declined to provide the information
  • CANCEL - The operation was cancelled

You can optionally have the client fill in missing values from the schema's default declarations before returning an accepted result to the server:

var client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .applyElicitationDefaults(true)   // default is false
    .elicitation(formElicitationHandler)
    .build();

When enabled, any keys absent from an accepted ElicitResult.content are populated with the default values declared in the request's requestedSchema.

docs.title: URL Elicitation Required Handling
docs.text:
When a server requires out-of-band URL elicitation but the client has not negotiated support for it (or the server strictly requires out-of-band handling), the server may return a URL_ELICITATION_REQUIRED error during tool execution or prompt retrieval.

try {
    mcpClient.callTool(new McpSchema.CallToolRequest("tool1", Map.of()));
} catch (McpError e) {
    if (e.getJsonRpcError().code() == McpSchema.ErrorCodes.URL_ELICITATION_REQUIRED) {
        // Extract elicitation requests from the error data
        Map<String, Object> data = (Map<String, Object>) e.getJsonRpcError().data();
        TypeRef<List<McpSchema.ElicitUrlRequest>> typeRef = new TypeRef<>() {};
        var requests = McpJsonDefaults.getMapper()
                .convertValue(data.get("elicitations"), typeRef);

        for (var req : requests) {
            // handle elicitation requests
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Elicitation Complete Notification (SEP-1036)
docs.text:
After a user finishes an out-of-band URL elicitation flow (for example, completing an OAuth authorization in a browser), the server sends a notifications/elicitation/complete message so the client knows it can stop waiting and re-check the outcome. Register a consumer to receive it:

var client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .capabilities(ClientCapabilities.builder()
        .elicitation(true, true)
        .build())
    .urlElicitation(urlElicitationHandler)
    .elicitationCompleteConsumer(notification -> {
        System.out.println("Elicitation " + notification.elicitationId() + " completed, re-checking outcome");
    })
    .build();

On the server side, send the notification once the out-of-band flow resolves (e.g. after the user completes the OAuth redirect), using the ID assigned to the original ElicitUrlRequest and the session that issued it:

server.sendElicitationComplete(exchange.sessionId(),
    new McpSchema.ElicitationCompleteNotification("oauth-123"));

docs.title: Logging Support
docs.text:
The client can register a logging consumer to receive log messages from the server and set the minimum logging level to filter messages:

var mcpClient = McpClient.sync(transport)
        .loggingConsumer(notification -> {
            System.out.println("Received log message: " + notification.data());
        })
        .build();

mcpClient.initialize();

mcpClient.setLoggingLevel(McpSchema.LoggingLevel.INFO);

// Call the tool that sends logging notifications
CallToolResult result = mcpClient.callTool(CallToolRequest.builder("logging-test").build());

Clients can control the minimum logging level they receive through the mcpClient.setLoggingLevel(level) request. Messages below the set level will be filtered out. Supported logging levels (in order of increasing severity): DEBUG (0), INFO (1), NOTICE (2), WARNING (3), ERROR (4), CRITICAL (5), ALERT (6), EMERGENCY (7)

docs.title: Progress Notifications
docs.text:
The client can register a progress consumer to track the progress of long-running operations:

var mcpClient = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .progressConsumer(progress -> {
        System.out.println("Progress: " + progress.progress() + "/" + progress.total());
    })
    .build();

docs.title: Pinging the Server
docs.text:
The client can send a ping request to check that the server is alive and responsive:

McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport).build();
client.initialize();

Object result = client.ping(); // blocks until the server responds, or the request times out

The async equivalent, McpAsyncClient.ping(), returns a Mono<Object> that completes when the server responds.

docs.title: Request Timeouts and Cancellation
docs.text:
Every request the client sends (callTool, readResource, ping, etc.) is bounded by the requestTimeout configured on the client builder (default 20 seconds):

McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .requestTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .build();

If a response doesn't arrive within that window, the pending call fails with a timeout error (an McpError on the sync API, or an error signal on the corresponding Mono for the async API) instead of blocking indefinitely. The server builder has an equivalent requestTimeout(Duration) option (default 10 hours) bounding requests the server sends to the client, such as sampling or elicitation.

The SDK does not currently send or process the MCP notifications/cancelled message, so timing out a request only stops the caller from waiting on it — it does not notify the other side that the in-flight operation should stop executing.

docs.title: Tool Execution
docs.text:
Tools are server-side functions that clients can discover and execute. The MCP client provides methods to list available tools and execute them with specific parameters. Each tool has a unique name and accepts a map of parameters.

Sync APIAsync API 
// List available tools
ListToolsResult tools = client.listTools();

// Call a tool with a CallToolRequest
CallToolResult result = client.callTool(
    CallToolRequest.builder("calculator")
        .arguments(Map.of(
            "operation", "add",
            "a", 1,
            "b", 2
        ))
        .build()
);

// List available tools asynchronously
client.listTools()
    .doOnNext(tools -> tools.tools().forEach(tool ->
        System.out.println(tool.name())))
    .subscribe();

// Call a tool asynchronously
client.callTool(CallToolRequest.builder("calculator")
        .arguments(Map.of(
            "operation", "add",
            "a", 1,
            "b", 2
        ))
        .build())
    .subscribe();

docs.title: Tool Schema Validation and Caching
docs.text:
The client supports optional JSON schema validation for tool call results and automatic schema caching:

var client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .jsonSchemaValidator(myValidator)            // Enable schema validation
    .enableCallToolSchemaCaching(true)           // Cache tool schemas
    .build();

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
listTools, listResources, listResourceTemplates, and listPrompts all accept an optional opaque cursor string, and their results carry a nextCursor that is non-null while more pages remain. Loop until nextCursor is null to collect every page:

List<McpSchema.Tool> allTools = new ArrayList<>();
String cursor = null;
do {
    ListToolsResult page = client.listTools(cursor);
    allTools.addAll(page.tools());
    cursor = page.nextCursor();
} while (cursor != null);

Each paginated method also accepts an optional _meta map alongside the cursor, e.g. client.listTools(cursor, Map.of("key", "value")), for passing request metadata through to the server.

docs.title: Resource Access
docs.text:
Resources represent server-side data sources that clients can access using URI templates. The MCP client provides methods to discover available resources and retrieve their contents through a standardized interface.

Sync APIAsync API 
// List available resources
ListResourcesResult resources = client.listResources();

// Read a resource
ReadResourceResult resource = client.readResource(
    ReadResourceRequest.builder("resource://uri").build()
);

// List available resources asynchronously
client.listResources()
    .doOnNext(resources -> resources.resources().forEach(resource ->
        System.out.println(resource.name())))
    .subscribe();

// Read a resource asynchronously
client.readResource(ReadResourceRequest.builder("resource://uri").build())
    .subscribe();

docs.title: Resource Subscriptions
docs.text:
When the server advertises resources.subscribe support, clients can subscribe to individual resources and receive a callback whenever the server pushes a notifications/resources/updated notification for that URI. The SDK automatically re-reads the resource on notification and delivers the updated contents to the registered consumer.

Register a consumer on the client builder, then subscribe/unsubscribe at any time:

Sync APIAsync API 
McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(transport)
    .resourcesUpdateConsumer(contents -> {
        // called with the updated resource contents after each notification
        System.out.println("Resource updated: " + contents);
    })
    .build();

client.initialize();

// Subscribe to a specific resource URI
client.subscribeResource(McpSchema.SubscribeRequest.builder("custom://resource").build());

// ... later, stop receiving updates
client.unsubscribeResource(McpSchema.UnsubscribeRequest.builder("custom://resource").build());

McpAsyncClient client = McpClient.async(transport)
    .resourcesUpdateConsumer(contents -> Mono.fromRunnable(() -> {
        System.out.println("Resource updated: " + contents);
    }))
    .build();

client.initialize()
    .then(client.subscribeResource(McpSchema.SubscribeRequest.builder("custom://resource").build()))
    .subscribe();

// ... later, stop receiving updates
client.unsubscribeResource(McpSchema.UnsubscribeRequest.builder("custom://resource").build())
    .subscribe();

docs.title: Prompt System
docs.text:
The prompt system enables interaction with server-side prompt templates. These templates can be discovered and executed with custom parameters, allowing for dynamic text generation based on predefined patterns.

Sync APIAsync API 
// List available prompt templates
ListPromptsResult prompts = client.listPrompts();

// Get a prompt with parameters
GetPromptResult prompt = client.getPrompt(
    GetPromptRequest.builder("greeting").arguments(Map.of("name", "World")).build()
);

// List available prompt templates asynchronously
client.listPrompts()
    .doOnNext(prompts -> prompts.prompts().forEach(prompt ->
        System.out.println(prompt.name())))
    .subscribe();

// Get a prompt asynchronously
client.getPrompt(GetPromptRequest.builder("greeting").arguments(Map.of("name", "World")).build())
    .subscribe();

docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to the Model Context Protocol Java SDK! This guide outlines how to contribute to this project.

Required Software

docs.text:
1. Fork the repository

  2. Clone your fork:

    git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/java-sdk.git
cd java-sdk

  3. Build from source:

    ./mvnw clean install -DskipTests  # skip the tests
./mvnw test                        # run tests

docs.title: Reporting Issues
docs.text: Please create an issue in the repository if you discover a bug or would like to propose an enhancement. Bug reports should have a reproducer in the form of a code sample or a repository attached that the maintainers or contributors can work with to address the problem.

docs.title: Making Changes
docs.text:
1. Create a new branch:

    git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name

  2. Make your changes.

  3. Validate your changes:

    ./mvnw clean test

docs.title: Principles of MCP
docs.text:
1. Simple + Minimal: It is much easier to add things to the codebase than it is to remove them. To maintain simplicity, we keep a high bar for adding new concepts and primitives as each addition requires maintenance and compatibility consideration.
  2. Concrete: Code changes need to be based on specific usage and implementation challenges and not on speculative ideas. Most importantly, the SDK is meant to implement the MCP specification.

docs.title: Submitting Changes
docs.text:
1. For non-trivial changes, please clarify with the maintainers in an issue whether you can contribute the change and the desired scope of the change.
  2. For trivial changes (for example a couple of lines or documentation changes) there is no need to open an issue first.
  3. Push your changes to your fork.
  4. Submit a pull request to the main repository.
  5. Follow the pull request template.
  6. Wait for review.
  7. For any follow-up work, please add new commits instead of force-pushing. This will allow the reviewer to focus on incremental changes instead of having to restart the review process.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The MCP Java SDK lets Java applications act as MCP clients and MCP servers. It requires Java 17 or later.

The SDK contains two implementations of the client and the server, one for each lifecycle model of the protocol:

  • Modern, for the 2026-07-28 specification. There is no handshake and no session; every request stands alone.
  • Legacy, for the 2025-11-25 specification and earlier revisions. Client and server set up a session with an initialize handshake.

The names come from the MCP specification. Legacy does not mean deprecated here: the SDK supports both generations. Both ship in the same mcp-core module, and an application can use both side by side.

docs.title: Modern or Legacy?
docs.text:
Choose by what the other side speaks. A modern client cannot call a legacy server, and a legacy client cannot call a modern server.

Modern Legacy Spec revision 2026-07-28 2025-11-25 and earlier Package io.modelcontextprotocol.modern io.modelcontextprotocol.client, io.modelcontextprotocol.server Lifecycle None: every request carries the protocol version and capabilities initialize handshake, then a session Requests from the server None: the server answers "input required" and the client sends the request again Sampling, elicitation, roots, ping Client instances One per user, sharing a transport One per server Scaling a server Any instance can answer any request Sessions live in the server process, except with the stateless server type Transports STDIO, Streamable HTTP STDIO, Streamable HTTP, SSE (deprecated) Spring transports Yes, in Spring AI 2.1+ Yes, in Spring AI 2.0+ Guides Client, Server Client, Server

docs.title: Modern Architecture
docs.text:
The 2026-07-28 revision removes sessions and the initialize handshake. The modern client and server are built around that and share no types with the legacy ones:

  • Client/Server Layer (McpClient/McpServer): The client turns each call into a self-contained request. The server dispatches each request to a feature, which calls a repository you implement.
  • No Session Layer: Every request carries the protocol version and the client's capabilities in its _meta, so any server instance can answer any request.
  • Transport Layer: Carries one request and its answer, which is a single response or a stream of notifications followed by the response, over:
    • STDIO
    • Streamable HTTP (JDK HttpClient on the client, Servlet on the server)

docs.title: Client
docs.text: A modern MCP client stands for one user. An application creates one client per user, and the clients of a server share one transport. Each call carries its user's context to the transport, which adds it to the request.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: A modern MCP server keeps nothing between requests. Over Streamable HTTP, any number of identical instances can serve the same clients without sticky routing. Over STDIO the client starts the server as a process of its own.

docs.title: Key Interactions
docs.text:
• No Initialization: Building a client does no I/O. The first request goes out when the first call starts.
  • Requests from the client: Tool discovery and calls, resource discovery and reading, prompts, completions, and server/discover for the server's capabilities.
  • Input from the user: The server cannot send requests to the client. A server that needs input answers with an input_required result, and the client sends the request again with the answers.
  • Change notifications: The client opens a subscriptions/listen stream, and the server reports list changes and resource updates on it.

See MCP Client (2026-07-28) and MCP Server (2026-07-28).

docs.title: Legacy Architecture
docs.text:
The legacy client and server keep a session between them, set up with an initialize handshake:

  • Client/Server Layer (McpClient/McpServer): The API you program against, in sync and async variants. McpClient handles the client-side protocol operations and McpServer the server-side ones.
  • Session Layer (McpSession): Manages communication patterns and state. It matches requests with responses, in both directions, for as long as the connection lasts.
  • Transport Layer (McpTransport): Handles JSON-RPC message serialization and delivery over:
    • STDIO (stdin/stdout)
    • Streamable HTTP (JDK HttpClient on the client, Servlet on the server)
    • SSE, the deprecated HTTP transport (JDK HttpClient on the client, Servlet on the server)
    • Spring WebFlux and Spring WebMVC transports (available in Spring AI 2.0+)

docs.title: Client
docs.text: An application creates one MCP client per server it uses. Each client holds its own session: to a remote server over Streamable HTTP or SSE, or to a local server process over STDIO.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: A legacy MCP server keeps one session per connected client, inside the server process. Over HTTP it runs in a web container. Over STDIO the client starts it as a process of its own.

docs.title: Key Interactions
docs.text:
• Initialization: Transport setup, protocol compatibility check, capability negotiation, and implementation details exchange.
  • Requests from the client: Tool discovery and calls, resource discovery and reading, prompts, and completions.
  • Requests from the server: Sampling, elicitation and roots listing, sent to the client over the same session.
  • Notifications: List changes, resource updates, progress, and logging.

See MCP Client and MCP Server.

docs.title: Module Structure
docs.text:
The SDK is organized into modules to separate concerns and allow adopters to bring in only what they need. All of them use the group io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:

Module Purpose mcp-bom Bill of Materials for dependency management mcp-core The modern and legacy clients and servers, with the STDIO, JDK HttpClient and Servlet transports mcp-json-jackson2 Jackson 2.x JSON serialization implementation mcp-json-jackson3 Jackson 3.x JSON serialization implementation mcp Convenience bundle (mcp-core + mcp-json-jackson3) mcp-test Shared testing utilities and integration tests

Tip

A minimal adopter may depend only on mcp (core + Jackson 3).

Spring-based applications that use the legacy client or server should use the mcp-spring-webflux or mcp-spring-webmvc artifacts from Spring AI 2.0+ (group org.springframework.ai), which are no longer part of this SDK. For the modern client and server, Spring AI 2.1+ provides Boot starters and Spring transports; see MCP Client Boot Starter and MCP 2026-07-28 Servers.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Add the SDK to your build, then make a first call to an MCP server. The SDK requires Java 17 or later.

docs.title: Bill of Materials (BOM)
docs.text:
Import the BOM so that all SDK modules use the same version and the dependencies below need no version of their own:

MavenGradle 
<dependencyManagement>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk</groupId>
            <artifactId>mcp-bom</artifactId>
            <version>2.1.0</version>
            <type>pom</type>
            <scope>import</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>

dependencies {
    implementation platform("io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp-bom:2.1.0")
}

Replace the version number with the latest version from Maven Central.

Note

The modern client and server, for the 2026-07-28 specification, are available from 2.2.0.

docs.title: SDK
docs.text:
Add the mcp module, which bundles mcp-core with Jackson 3.x JSON serialization:

MavenGradle 
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk</groupId>
    <artifactId>mcp</artifactId>
</dependency>

dependencies {
    implementation "io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp"
}

This is all a client needs. It includes the modern and the legacy client and server, with their STDIO and HTTP transports, and requires no web framework.

HTTP servers

The HTTP server transports are built on the Servlet API, which the SDK does not bring in. Run them in a Servlet container, such as Tomcat or Jetty, with async support enabled.

For the modern client and server, Spring AI 2.1+ provides Boot starters and Spring transports; see MCP Client Boot Starter and MCP 2026-07-28 Servers.

docs.title: Your First Client
docs.text:
The SDK has two clients, one for each generation of the protocol; see Modern or Legacy? to choose. Both examples list the tools of a server at http://localhost:8080/mcp and call one of them.

ModernLegacy

For servers of the 2026-07-28 specification. There is nothing to initialize and nothing to close on the client:

import java.util.Map;

import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.CallToolResult;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.McpClient;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.McpSyncClient;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.client.transport.HttpClientMcpTransport;

McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(
        HttpClientMcpTransport.builder("http://localhost:8080/mcp").build())
    .build();

client.listTools().list().tools().forEach(tool -> System.out.println(tool.name()));

CallToolResult result = client.tool("echo")
    .arguments(Map.of("text", "Hello"))
    .call();
System.out.println(result.content());

Continue with the MCP Client (2026-07-28) guide.

For servers of the 2025-11-25 specification and earlier. The client sets up a session with initialize():

import java.util.Map;

import io.modelcontextprotocol.client.McpClient;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.client.McpSyncClient;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.client.transport.HttpClientStreamableHttpTransport;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpSchema.CallToolRequest;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpSchema.CallToolResult;

McpSyncClient client = McpClient.sync(
        HttpClientStreamableHttpTransport.builder("http://localhost:8080").build())
    .build();

client.initialize();

client.listTools().tools().forEach(tool -> System.out.println(tool.name()));

CallToolResult result = client.callTool(
        CallToolRequest.builder("echo").arguments(Map.of("text", "Hello")).build());
System.out.println(result.content());

client.closeGracefully();

Continue with the MCP Client guide.

To build the server side, see the Quick Start of the modern server guide, which serves the echo tool the modern example calls, and the MCP Server guide for the legacy server.

The BOM manages the following modules, all in the group io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:

JSON binding is pluggable. mcp-json-jackson3 Jackson 3.x JSON serialization (included in mcp). mcp-json-jackson2 Jackson 2.x JSON serialization, for projects that need Jackson 2.x. mcp-test Testing utilities and support for MCP-based applications.

docs.title: MCP Server (2026-07-28)
docs.text:
Note

The modern server is available since 2.2.0. Its API, in the io.modelcontextprotocol.modern packages, may change in minor releases until 3.0, and some parts of the revision are not implemented. For clients that speak earlier revisions, use the legacy server. To call a modern server from Java, see the modern client.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The modern server implements the stateless 2026-07-28 MCP specification revision. It lives in io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server, next to the legacy server, and shares no types with it: it has its own McpServer, its own McpSchema, and its own transports. Both ship in mcp-core, so no extra dependency is needed.

The 2026-07-28 revision removes sessions and the initialize handshake. Every request carries the protocol version and client capabilities in its _meta, and the server answers each request on its own. The modern server is built around that:

  • No sessions. Any instance can serve any request, so a server scales out without sticky routing.
  • No server-to-client requests. A server that needs input from the user or the model answers with an InputRequiredResult, and the client retries the request with the answers (see Multi Round-Trip Requests).
  • Your catalog, your code. Tools, resources, prompts and completions come from repositories you implement, not from a registry inside the SDK. Per-tenant, filtered, dynamic and paginated catalogs need no extra API.
  • One server, sync or async. There is a single McpServer. You pick sync or async per repository; sync code never sees a Reactor type.
  • Stream only when needed. A handler returns a single result (sent as application/json) or a streaming body that can send progress before the result (sent as an SSE stream).

docs.title: Modern or legacy?
docs.text:
Modern server Legacy server Package io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server io.modelcontextprotocol.server Spec revision 2026-07-28 2025-11-25 and earlier Sessions No Yes (except the stateless transport) Primitives Repositories you implement Registered specifications Server-to-client requests Replaced by InputRequiredResult Sampling, elicitation, roots, ping Logging Not supported (deprecated by the revision) Supported

By default the modern server only accepts the 2026-07-28 protocol version; change the set with supportedVersions(...) on the builder. A request declaring another version gets an Unsupported protocol version error listing the versions the server supports. Clients that start with an initialize handshake are not supported; serve those with the legacy server.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
A server with one tool, served over HTTP:

SyncAsync 
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.CallToolResult;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.Implementation;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.TextContent;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.Tool;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.McpRequestContext;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.McpServer;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.McpSyncResponse;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.feature.McpSyncTool;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.feature.McpSyncToolRepository;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.feature.ToolsFeature;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.feature.ToolsPage;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.transport.HttpServletMcpTransport;

class EchoTools implements McpSyncToolRepository {

    private final McpSyncTool echo = McpSyncTool.of(
            Tool.builder("echo", Map.of(
                    "type", "object",
                    "properties", Map.of("text", Map.of("type", "string")),
                    "required", List.of("text")))
                .description("Echoes the given text")
                .build(),
            (ctx, request) -> McpSyncResponse.result(CallToolResult.builder()
                .addContent(TextContent.builder((String) request.arguments().get("text")).build())
                .build()));

    @Override
    public ToolsPage list(McpRequestContext ctx, String cursor) {
        return ToolsPage.of(List.of(this.echo.definition()));
    }

    @Override
    public McpSyncTool find(McpRequestContext ctx, String name) {
        return "echo".equals(name) ? this.echo : null;
    }

}

McpServer server = McpServer.builder()
    .serverInfo(Implementation.builder("echo-server", "1.0.0").build())
    .feature(ToolsFeature.ofSync(new EchoTools()))
    .build();

HttpServletMcpTransport transport = HttpServletMcpTransport.builder(server)
    .endpoint("/mcp")
    .build();

// Register `transport` as a servlet in your container, mapped to /mcp,
// with async support enabled.

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.CallToolResult;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.Implementation;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.TextContent;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.McpSchema.Tool;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.McpAsyncResponse;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.McpRequestContext;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.McpServer;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.feature.McpAsyncTool;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.feature.McpAsyncToolRepository;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.feature.ToolsFeature;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.feature.ToolsPage;
import io.modelcontextprotocol.modern.server.transport.HttpServletMcpTransport;
import reactor.core.publisher.Mono;

class EchoTools implements McpAsyncToolRepository {

    private final McpAsyncTool echo = McpAsyncTool.of(
            Tool.builder("echo", Map.of(
                    "type", "object",
                    "properties", Map.of("text", Map.of("type", "string")),
                    "required", List.of("text")))
                .description("Echoes the given text")
                .build(),
            (ctx, request) -> Mono.just(McpAsyncResponse.result(CallToolResult.builder()
                .addContent(TextContent.builder((String) request.arguments().get("text")).build())
                .build())));

    @Override
    public Mono<ToolsPage> list(McpRequestContext ctx, String cursor) {
        return Mono.just(ToolsPage.of(List.of(this.echo.definition())));
    }

    @Override
    public Mono<McpAsyncTool> find(McpRequestContext ctx, String name) {
        return "echo".equals(name) ? Mono.just(this.echo) : Mono.empty();
    }

}

McpServer server = McpServer.builder()
    .serverInfo(Implementation.builder("echo-server", "1.0.0").build())
    .feature(ToolsFeature.ofAsync(new EchoTools()))
    .build();

HttpServletMcpTransport transport = HttpServletMcpTransport.builder(server)
    .endpoint("/mcp")
    .build();

// Register `transport` as a servlet in your container, mapped to /mcp,
// with async support enabled.

McpServer is immutable and stateless. build() collects the capabilities of the registered features and serves server/discover from them. There is nothing to start; on shutdown, server.closeGracefully() ends open subscriptions/listen streams with a complete result (see Change Notifications).

Builder options:

Method Purpose serverInfo(Implementation) Required. Sent in _meta of every result. instructions(String) Instructions for the model, returned by server/discover. feature(McpFeature) / features(List) Register tools, resources, prompts, completions or a custom feature. subscriptions(McpChangePublisher) Enable subscriptions/listen. See Change Notifications. requestStateCodec(RequestStateCodec) Seal requestState. See Securing requestState. discoverCache(long ttlMs, CacheScope) Caching hints for server/discover. See Caching. supportedVersions(List<String>) Protocol versions to accept. Defaults to 2026-07-28. jsonMapper(McpJsonMapper) JSON mapper. Defaults to McpJsonDefaults.getMapper().

docs.title: Streamable HTTP (Servlet)
docs.text:
HttpServletMcpTransport is a Jakarta Servlet. It accepts POST only, one request or notification per call. Requests are served on the container thread, so thread-locals set by servlet filters (security context, tracing) are visible to sync handlers. subscriptions/listen streams are served asynchronously, so the servlet and all filters in front of it must support async requests.

HttpServletMcpTransport transport = HttpServletMcpTransport.builder(server)
    .endpoint("/mcp")
    .contextExtractor(request -> request.getUserPrincipal() == null ? McpTransportContext.EMPTY
            : McpTransportContext.create(Map.of("user", request.getUserPrincipal().getName())))
    .httpHeaderValidator(DefaultServerTransportSecurityValidator.builder()
        .allowedOrigin("https://app.example.com")
        .allowedHost("mcp.example.com")
        .build())
    .keepAliveInterval(Duration.ofSeconds(15))
    .build();
Method Default Purpose endpoint(String) /mcp The path the transport answers on. contextExtractor(...) empty context Builds the McpTransportContext handlers see. Runs on the container thread before dispatch. httpHeaderValidator(...) rejects any Origin Validates headers before the body is read. See HTTP Security. maxRequestSize(int) 16 MiB Maximum request body size. keepAliveInterval(Duration) 30 seconds SSE comment interval on open streams; also detects clients that went away. null disables it. errorStatus(int code, int status) see below HTTP status for a JSON-RPC error code.

JSON-RPC errors are answered with the HTTP status the specification assigns: 400 for parse errors, invalid requests, invalid params, header mismatches, missing client capabilities and unsupported protocol versions, and 404 for unknown methods. Other codes are answered with 200. Once a stream has started, errors are sent in-band.

Call transport.closeGracefully() on shutdown. It stops accepting requests and also calls server.closeGracefully(), which ends open subscriptions/listen streams with a complete result.

The servlet requires the routing headers the 2026-07-28 HTTP transport defines, and checks them against the request body:

  • Mcp-Method is required on every request and must equal the JSON-RPC method.
  • MCP-Protocol-Version is required when the body declares a protocol version in _meta, and must match it.
  • Mcp-Name is required on tools/call and prompts/get (the name) and resources/read (the uri), and must match it.

A request with a missing or mismatched header is rejected with error -32020 (header mismatch, HTTP 400) before it is dispatched. Filters can therefore route or authorize on these headers without reading the body. Keep this in mind when testing with curl or another hand-written client.

docs.title: STDIO
docs.text:
StdioMcpTransport reads one JSON-RPC message per line from stdin and writes responses to stdout. Requests are handled concurrently, cancellation is supported, and a single writer keeps output lines intact.

StdioMcpTransport transport = new StdioMcpTransport(server, McpJsonDefaults.getMapper());

// Serve until stdin is closed or closeGracefully() is called.
transport.start().block();

The transport's threads are daemon threads, so block on start() to keep the process alive. Messages longer than 16M characters are dropped; use the five-argument constructor to change the limit.

Unlike the Servlet transport, StdioMcpTransport.closeGracefully() does not call server.closeGracefully(): it cancels in-flight requests, including open subscriptions/listen streams, without sending their pending output. If you use change notifications, call server.closeGracefully() before closing the transport.

STDIO has no headers and no contextExtractor: handlers always see a transport context without user entries, so anything that reads identity from transportContext(), such as a requestState principal binding, has nothing to read.

docs.title: Spring
docs.text: Spring WebMVC and WebFlux transports for the modern server, and a Boot starter that configures it, are part of Spring AI 2.1+, not of this SDK. See MCP 2026-07-28 Servers in the Spring AI reference.

docs.title: HTTP Security
docs.text:
Authentication and authorization belong in servlet filters in front of HttpServletMcpTransport, including 401/403 challenges. To pass the authenticated identity to handlers, read it in the contextExtractor and put it in the McpTransportContext.

Against DNS rebinding, the transport validates headers with a ServerHttpHeaderValidator before reading the body. The default validator has no allowed origins and no allowed hosts, which means:

  • A request without an Origin header (a non-browser client) passes.
